technical.summary: ACN shows strong directional bias with bullish moving average alignment and Ichimoku cross-up, but overbought oscillators (RSI-9, Stoch-K) and weak volume profile limit swing entry conviction at current levels.

fundamental.summary: ACN shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signal, zero government contract activity, no lobbying engagement, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 73 days present material risk with insufficient fundamental support.

sentiment.summary: Mixed signals: modest congressional buying (junior members, small amounts) offset by one sale; greed sentiment suggests caution; no news data to confirm setup; overall neutral stance warranted.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (95.48) indicates extreme market stress; earnings in 73 days adds event risk but is not imminent; falling DXY provides modest relief for multinational ACN.

debate.key_bull_argument: Ichimoku cross-up with price above all major moving averages and supertrend bullish provides directional confirmation for swing entry near support at 301.41.
debate.key_bear_argument: Extreme overbought conditions (RSI-9 at 72, Stoch-K at 93.69), weak volume (0.82 ratio), negative CMF, inverted yield curve, VIX crisis levels (95.48), and zero fundamental support create exhaustion risk with unfavorable macro backdrop.

decision.entry_rationale: Technical setup shows Ichimoku cross-up and price above major moving averages, but overbought oscillators (RSI-9 72, Stoch-K 93.69) signal exhaustion at resistance. decision.primary_risk: Extreme overbought conditions combined with VIX crisis and inverted yield curve create high probability of mean reversion or gap down on macro deterioration; earnings in 73 days adds uncompensated event risk.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bearish bias despite technical bullish signals
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding ACN position with 14 existing IT sector positions (19% of portfolio); concentration risk and sector saturation argue against adding exposure.
